pairs: Et iterum cœpit docere ad mare:
And again, he began to teach by the sea.
et congregata est ad eum turba multa,
And a great crowd was gathered to him, so much so that,
ita ut navim ascendens sederet in mari,
climbing into a boat, he was seated on the sea.
et omnis turba circa mare super terram erat:
And the entire crowd was on the land along the sea.
et docebat eos in parabolis multa,
And he taught them many things in parables,
et dicebat illis in doctrina sua:
and he said to them, in his doctrine:
Behold, the sower went out to sow.
and the birds of the air came
Yet truly, others fell upon stony ground,
where it did not have much soil.
because it had no depth of soil.
And when the sun was risen,
et eo quod non habebat radicem,
And because it had no root,
and it did not produce fruit.
Et aliud cecidit in terram bonam:
And some fell on good soil.
et dabat fructum ascendentem et crescentem,
And it brought forth fruit that grew up, and increased,
some sixty, and some one hundred.”
And when he was alone, the twelve,
interrogaverunt eum hi qui cum eo erant duodecim, parabolam.
who were with him, questioned him about the parable.
Vobis datum est nosse mysterium regni Dei:
it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God.
But to those who are outside,
and not understand; lest at any time they may be converted,
and their sins would be forgiven them.’”
And so, how will you understand all the parables?
Hi autem sunt, qui circa viam,
Now there are those who are along the way,
And when they have heard it,
confestim venit Satanas, et aufert verbum,
Satan quickly comes and takes away the word,
quod seminatum est in cordibus eorum.
which was sown in their hearts.
Et hi sunt similiter, qui super petrosa seminantur:
And similarly, there are those who were sown upon stony ground.
These, when they have heard the word,
et non habent radicem in se,
But they have no root in themselves,
and so they are for a limited time.
deinde orta tribulatione et persecutione propter verbum,
And when next tribulation and persecution arises because of the word,
Et alii sunt qui in spinas seminantur:
And there are others who are sown among thorns.
These are those who hear the word,
et circa reliqua concupiscentiæ introëuntes suffocant verbum,
and desires about other things enter in and suffocate the word,
and it is effectively without fruit.
Et hi sunt qui super terram bonam seminati sunt,
And there are those who are sown upon good soil,
Numquid venit lucerna ut sub modio ponatur,
“Would someone enter with a lamp in order to place it under a basket
Would it not be placed upon a lampstand?
Non est enim aliquid absconditum, quod non manifestetur:
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed.
Neither was anything done in secret,
except that it may be made public.
If anyone has ears to hear,
With whatever measure you have measured out,
it shall be measured back to you,
and more shall be added to you.
to him it shall be given.
etiam quod habet auferetur ab eo.
from him even what he has shall be taken away.”
“The kingdom of God is like this:
quemadmodum si homo jaciat sementem in terram,
it is as if a man were to cast seed on the land.
And he sleeps and he arises,
And the seed germinates and grows,
though he does not know it.
For the earth bears fruit readily:
next the full grain in the ear.
And when the fruit has been produced,
immediately he sends out the sickle,
“To what should we compare the kingdom of God?
Or to what parable should we compare it?
Sicut granum sinapis, quod cum seminatum fuerit in terra,
It is like a grain of mustard seed which, when it has been sown in the earth,
minus est omnibus seminibus, quæ sunt in terra:
is less than all the seeds which are in the earth.
and becomes greater than all the plants,
ita ut possint sub umbra ejus aves cæli habitare.
so much so that the birds of the air are able to live under its shadow.”
Et talibus multis parabolis loquebatur eis verbum,
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them,
as much as they were able to hear.
sine parabola autem non loquebatur eis:
But he did not speak to them without a parable.
seorsum autem discipulis suis disserebat omnia.
Yet separately, he explained all things to his disciples.
Et ait illis in illa die,
And on that day, when evening had arrived,
assumunt eum ita ut erat in navi:
they brought him, so that he was in one boat,
et aliæ naves erant cum illo.
and other boats were with him.
Et facta est procella magna venti,
And a great wind storm occurred,
and the waves broke over the boat,
so that the boat was being filled.
Et erat ipse in puppi super cervical dormiens:
And he was in the stern of the boat,
does it not concern you that we are perishing?”
And rising up, he rebuked the wind,
and he said to the sea: “Silence.
And they were struck with a great fear.
And they said to one another,
quia et ventus et mare obediunt ei?
that both wind and sea obey him?”
